analysis: Broad Future Earth response retains biology, field-based Earth and soil study, remote sensing, food, water and complementary empirical tools. Marine Biology restores direct aquatic content while leaving the cross-major coastal project visibly separate.

Governance route brings together comparative politics, international law, environmental justice, public economics, EU institutions, civil society and climate communication with climate, resources and spatial observation. It draws on Future Society interests without purporting to reproduce that major.

The required energy-transition interest supports a composition with energy resource assessment, renewable system design, life-cycle analysis, materials recovery and environmental resources, plus enterprise, leadership and market methods. Business study adds implementation perspectives; energy and environmental evidence remain central.

scopedReassessment: ENSSUST313 is available only in the initial semester. Moving the advanced team project there would precede the intended methods and environmental foundations. Marine Biology, Contemporary Social Theory and Market Research offer the respective compositions substantive alternatives. Energy & Sustainability displaces Business & Economy in the Age of AI because energy technology and systems have closer support. Tested alternative plans and retained current worksheet offerings. Course descriptions were considered fully where no outline exists.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce complex sustainability challenges and systems thinking; the UvA course includes a first academic paper.
Both examine Earth-system processes. UCR concentrates on geology and geophysics, while UvA also integrates biology and chemistry.
Both examine climate-system processes, impacts, sea-level change and societal responses.
Both address ecosystems and biodiversity; the UvA course connects global biomes explicitly to food supply.
Both address natural hazards and their impacts. UvA explicitly uses Google Earth Pro to study spatial patterns.
Both develop remote-sensing and spatial-data methods for environmental change.
Both study soil properties and their environmental significance; the UvA course focuses specifically on plant-soil relations in food systems.
Both critically examine sustainable alternatives to industrial agriculture.
Both study water availability, hydrological processes, management and adaptation.
The compulsory Future Earth laboratory and field practical has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
Both study aquatic life and ecosystems. Marine Biology concentrates on marine settings; UvA explicitly connects aquatic science, human impacts and restoration.
The preparatory environmental-data course tied to the Desertification field course has no separate UCR equivalent.
The dedicated field course in geo-ecological mapping and desertification has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
Both design responses to water-related sustainability challenges. UvA explicitly teaches scenario planning, while Building with Nature explores design using natural processes.
Both examine how science, politics, institutions and society shape sustainability transitions.
Both consider how environmental conditions affect communities. UCR focuses on social movements and environmental justice; UvA takes a broader quality-of-life perspective.
Both address externalities, public policy and welfare. UvA focuses directly on environmental pollution and climate economics.
Both compare energy sources and transitions through technical, economic and environmental perspectives.
Both teach research design. UvA’s course supports the parallel Bachelor Project, while UCR’s course introduces empirical design and statistics.
Both use R to work with and visualise data. UvA also introduces formal statistical inference.
Both develop statistical models, uncertainty estimation and hypothesis testing.
UvA requires a collaborative interdisciplinary coastal project. UCR includes applied methods and field study across several courses.
The dedicated group research course combining interviews and surveys around quality of life has no single ordinary UCR equivalent.
The compulsory programme-specific philosophy-of-science course has no single course in these UCR schedules.
The dedicated R programming course has no separate ordinary-course equivalent in these UCR schedules.
The genuine 30-EC elective semester remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.
The compulsory 18-EC individual Bachelor Project cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or as UCR's optional comparison-only research element.
